seoTitle: Redirect Chain and Loop Finder for Redirect Lists
metaDescription: Paste old to new redirect pairs and find chains and loops, then get flattened rules that point every old URL straight to its final destination.
intro: Checks a redirect list for chains (A to B to C) and loops (A to B to A) and outputs rules where each old URL goes directly to the final URL.
why:
Migrations pile redirects on redirects. Each extra hop slows visitors and wastes crawl effort, and Google advises keeping chains to three hops or fewer. A loop breaks the page completely.

This tool works on the list you paste, so you can fix the map before it goes live. To follow redirects on a real URL, use the Redirect Chain Analyzer with curl output. Matching uses host, path and query exactly as written, with an option to ignore the trailing slash.
howTo: Paste your redirect pairs, one per line.
Copy the flattened rules and replace the old list.

faq.a: A rule whose target is itself the source of another rule. The tool follows it to the end.
They are listed and left out of the flattened rules, because they have no valid destination. Fix them by hand.
No. It only reads the list you paste.

faq.q: How many hops does Google follow?
faq.a: Up to 10, but its site move guide advises three at most in practice.
